t.2.108.1: When Bharata had gone back, Rāma, dwelling in the forest of ascetics, then noticed the alarm and the restless anxiety of the ascetics.
t.2.108.2: Those who lived there in the ascetics' hermitage in front of Citrakūṭa, content in their devotions under Rāma's protection, he noticed had grown restless and uneasy.
t.2.108.3: Apprehensive, they pointed at Rāma with their eyes and with frowning brows, and whispering to one another, they quietly held secret conversations among themselves.
t.2.108.4: Noticing their anxiety, Rāma, suspecting that he himself was the cause, then joined his palms and spoke these words to the seer, the head of the community.
t.2.108.5: Venerable one, surely nothing of my former conduct is now seen in me to have changed for the worse, on account of which the ascetics are troubled?
t.2.108.6: Has my younger brother Lakṣmaṇa, through carelessness, done anything that the sages have seen as unbefitting of himself?
t.2.108.8: Then the sage, aged by years and worn to frailty by his austerities, spoke as if trembling to Rāma, who was devoted to compassion for all beings.
t.2.108.7: Has Sītā, while attending upon you and devoted to serving me, perhaps failed to conduct herself fittingly, in the manner proper to a woman?
t.2.108.10: It is on your account that this trouble now befalls the ascetics; therefore, alarmed by the rākṣasas, they talk anxiously among themselves.
t.2.108.9: How, dear sir, could there be any lapse in conduct on the part of Vaidehī, whose nature is noble and who delights in what is good, and especially toward ascetics?
t.2.108.11: Here there is a certain rākṣasa named Khara, the younger brother of Rāvaṇa, who, having uprooted all the ascetics dwelling in Janasthāna…
t.2.108.12: Bold and swaggering with victory, cruel, a devourer of men, arrogant and wicked, he cannot bear you either, dear son.
t.2.108.13: Ever since you have been dwelling in this hermitage, dear son, from that very time the rākṣasas have been harassing the ascetics.
t.2.108.14: For they show themselves in loathsome, cruel and terrifying forms, in manifold and misshapen forms, forms that are painful to behold.
t.2.108.15: Defiling some ascetics by bringing them into contact with foul and impure things, those ignoble ones, standing right before them, swiftly strike down others.
t.2.108.16: In those various hermitage sites they lurk unnoticed, and there those small-minded ones take their pleasure in destroying the ascetics.
t.2.108.17: When the time for the oblation has come, they fling away the ladles and vessels, sprinkle the fires with water, and smash the pitchers.
t.2.108.18: Wishing to abandon their hermitages, which have been overrun by those evil-minded ones, the sages are today urging me to depart for another region.
t.2.108.20: Not far from here lies a lovely forest, rich in roots and fruits; together with my companions I shall once again take refuge in my old hermitage there.
t.2.108.19: Therefore, Rāma, before those wicked ones inflict bodily harm upon us ascetics, we shall abandon this hermitage.
t.2.108.21: Before long, dear son, Khara will turn to wrongdoing against you as well; come away from here with us, if your mind is so inclined.
t.2.108.23: To the ascetic who had spoken thus and was eager to depart, Rāma, the king's son, could not by any words in reply prevail to hold him back.
t.2.108.22: Since for one who is accompanied by his wife there is constant peril, O Rāghava, dwelling here now is a hardship for you, even though you are capable.
t.2.108.24: Having greeted Rāghava, taken leave of him, and reassured him, the head of the community abandoned the hermitage and departed together with the families.
t.2.108.25: Rāma, having accompanied the band of sages and seen them off, saluted the sage who was head of their community; then, permitted by them, who were thoroughly pleased, and instructed in what he should do, he returned from that place to his own holy dwelling to live there.
t.2.108.26: But the lord Rāghava did not leave the hermitage, now bereft of its seers, even for a moment, for ascetics who upheld the virtues of the seers' way of life constantly followed Rāghava.
